speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (a) what are the processes behind the development of guidelines and conditions for arts funding; (b) how frequently are such processes, guidelines and conditions reviewed; (c) when is the next review; (d) who are the stakeholders and actors that participate in the review process; and (e) to what degree are local artists consulted in these reviews.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Over the years, NAC has seen a growth in the number of deserving artists and arts companies.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Therefore, it must prioritise projects, given finite resources.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: For every individual grant application, artistic merit is an important criterion.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: NAC also takes into account the project's contribution to gaps and needs in the art form's development.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The extent to which it is able to engage audiences is also of consideration.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The criteria upon which funding applications are evaluated are available on NAC's website.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: NAC regularly convenes grants evaluation panels, comprising many members of the arts community, to give NAC their views on the proposal's artistic merit.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: Annually, over 400 arts practitioners, researchers, industry professionals and others are appointed to these panels.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: These assessors offer NAC objective feedback and help NAC identify emerging developments in the sector.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: NAC has benefited from their counsel and appreciates their continued support.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: In addition to regular engagement sessions and meetings with arts practitioners and groups on funding as well as on other issues of common interest, such as how to grow audiences, develop the various art forms and address the needs of freelancers, NAC also actively engages the arts community when embarking on major reviews of grant funding.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth (Mr Baey Yam Keng) (for the Minister for Culture, Community and Youth)
text: The revised Major Company Scheme was a response to the arts community's feedback on the need for a more customised approach that recognises different capabilities and contributions.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: And, if so, does the feedback suggest that artists agree with this rule?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Thirdly, perhaps, I missed this, but just to clarify: is there a timeline for reviewing these guidelines?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is there a fixed schedule, say, every three or five years, to review them and, if so, when is the next review scheduled to be held?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: As mentioned earlier in Parliament, the NAC does not fund activities that undermine public institutions, political parties or figures, regardless of political affiliation.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: NAC takes the position that the arts should not be used for partisan politics and that confidence in public institutions is fundamental to the future of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: We respect the views of artists and members of the arts community on this.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: But as a public institution, we also need to take into account the views and concerns of the public at large beyond the arts community.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This is a balance that we are striking and the position would, of course, need to evolve with the changes and needs of society, what the public can accept or not.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The conversation remains open and that is why we are constantly also reviewing our guidelines.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Currently, we will continue to review guidelines and engage artists in dialogue in order to understand their concerns and also to articulate the positions or the thinking of the Government.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: This reflects the shared ownership as well as responsibility in enlarging the space for our arts to flourish.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: The Parliamentary Secretary alluded to taking into consideration public sentiments.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: Is there any evidence that the general public is concerned about this issue that political parties or institutions should not be undermined via arts funding?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The views of the public are very diverse.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Based on our conversations not only with the arts groups, but also beyond the MCCY family, there are also considerations of the Government at large, on the role of Government and how public funds should be used to promote the various sectors to grow.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the case of the arts, artistic development is certainly of importance to us, but, at the same time, we also see the arts as a way to engage the community to build a stronger sense of national identity.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: Just to follow up on the same issue, so I would like to know what is the process like.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: For example, when there is a work that is deemed to be questionable, what is the process like to make the decisions?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In between, are there any recourse, are there any possibilities for dialogue?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: And a follow-up question would be: just this year, may I know how many projects or works have not been funded because of this guideline?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The NAC or any funding organisation will always have a conversation with the applicant.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In the case where there are some concerns over its content or the nature of the proposal, sometimes, it is about clarifications, about sharing the concerns, and the artist or applicant is always encouraged to respond accordingly and, if necessary, to make adjustments to the proposal, if the artist so desires.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: It is a continued exchange of views and there is a process where the applicant can appeal against the decision but NAC retains the final say on whether funding will be continued, withdrawn or the decision could be changed.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Was there a second part to the question?

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: How many projects or works have actually not been funded due to this ruling?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: In fact, very small numbers, compared to the thousands that we fund every year.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Can I just ask the Parliamentary Secretary whether the prohibition against the undermining of political parties includes political parties in the past?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: So,  is the Member alluding to current political parties or to parties no longer in existence?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Sorry, if I did not make myself clear.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I meant, does it include, for example, any funding for any proposed works that deal with political parties in our history, in the past that may present to some people a different interpretation of what the party did or did not do in the past?

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: The government of the day would need to decide on how money is used.

speaker: Mr Baey Yam Keng
text: Such that the works do not undermine the authority of public institutions under the government which is formed by the ruling party, which sets its policies for the government to operate.
